reason: Survives the feasibility lens. (1) Implementation is a few lines. In exp48 cell 8, write_test_submission (lines 1688-1748) applies max(0,int(round())) as the very LAST operation. Linefit, weak-leaf prune, DaughterNet insertion, the edge filter / stitch, relink, gap closing and safe divisions all run earlier on float coordinates. Nothing downstream consumes the written coordinates, so there is no conflict with any step, and node and edge sets are bit-identical. The x138 port is the same: DIFF.md line 52 confirms its CSV writer still rounds and its tail is already float. (2) The lab can test it exactly. The replay tail npz stores float post-linefit zyx (replay.py ~line 1436, 'pre-rounding'), and write_geff (lines 625-634) is the only rounding point, so a round_coords flag is enough. The official metric (tracksdata DistanceMatching and metrics.py) never rounds or casts coordinates. A confirmation replay is a cheap Kaggle CPU run with no GPU. The measured +0.0018 comes from an exact reimplementation (199/199 videos), divisions are unchanged, and it involves no network-trust optimism because detector nodes and probabilities are fixed and only the output quantisation changes. (3) Runtime cost at inference is zero. The CSV grows by about 12 bytes per node row (roughly +20%), which is harmless for a notebook output. (4) The only real feasibility hole is the probe decision rule. LB scores are read to 3 decimals, so a true +0.0012 shows as +0.001 or +0.002 and a +0.0006 may show as 0. Truncation by the hosted parser measured -0.0047 on 6bba but +0.0002 on 44b6. If the public test embryo behaves like 44b6, truncation looks the same as 'server rounds' on public (both about 0) while private (71%, other embryos) could lose about 0.004. The proposed rule 'same score -> harmless, keep' is therefore unsafe. The research's own >=55% win-rate gate also fails literally because 40-50% of videos tie exactly. Both are fixable, so the idea is not refuted.
fix_if_any: Change the decision rule, not the mechanism. (a) Run a dedicated probe = best-known submission with only BIOHUB_OUTPUT_FLOAT_COORDS=1. KEEP floats only if the displayed public score rises by >= +0.001. If it is unchanged, lower, or fails to parse, REVERT to int(round()): an unchanged score cannot tell 'server rounds' apart from 'server truncates on a 44b6-like embryo', and truncation costs about 0.004 on a 6bba-like private embryo. (b) Write every node coordinate with '%.3f' clipped to [0, dim-1]. Keep t, ids and the edge-row -1 values as ints so type inference is stable. (c) In the lab, use round_coords=False only for treatment arms, so exp39/exp48 controls still reproduce exactly. Gate on the D-weighted delta, the per-embryo 90% CI and the win rate among CHANGED videos, not the raw >=55%. (d) Bundle the change into later probes only after (a) has shown a gain. Run the float-aware linefit grid (6 CPU replays) only if time allows; it is optional.
realistic_public_gain: +0.001 (range 0 to +0.002) if the hosted parser keeps Float64. 0 if it rounds, in which case the change is reverted at no cost. The cost is one LB probe plus about 0.5 GPU-h for the notebook commit. Implementation plus the lab confirmation take under half a day.
